The Office for Product Safety & Standards (OPSS) said parents should stop using the MiniDream Organic 5-in-1 Baby Activity Gym immediately
What's On
Hannah Ahmed
08:50, 12 Jun 2025
The Office for Product Safety & Standards (OPSS) said parents should stop using the MiniDream Organic 5-in-1 Baby Activity Gym immediately
A popular £49 baby mat has been urgently recalled in
the UK over the risk of tots
choking as parents are told to "stop" using it "immediately".
The Office for Product Safety & Standards (OPSS) said parents should stop using the MiniDream Organic 5-in-1 Baby Activity Gym immediately, as it issued an urgent alert for new parents.
‌
The product presents a serious risk of entrapment as it includes fabric loops
which may entrap a child’s finger.
It also presents a high asphyxiation risk, due to internal fibrous filling which can be easily accessed, the statement warns mums and dads across the UK.
‌
READ MORE Households warned over supermarket item which has left 95 ill and 58 in hospital
The listing has been removed by the online marketplace, which in this case was Amazon. The product description is described as a "circular floor mat with cross-over arches with 5 detachable toys hanging from them. 1 teether ring, detachable from mat".
Article continues below
Local Authority Trading Standards said: "The product presents a serious risk of entrapment, as the detachable toys included fabric loops sewn into the side of one of the seams.
"The loops were large enough that a young child could easily insert their finger into them and twist, causing injuries.The product also presents a high risk of asphyxiation as the fabric on the star toy split at a lower than permissible force, allowing access to internal fibrous filling.
"A young child may place this filling in their mouth, causing them to choke and/or asphyxiate. The product does not meet the requirements of the Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011."
Article continues below
It went on, adding: "Owners should stop using the products immediately. Contact the distributor you purchased from to request redress."
The barcode affected is 5060727542240. In a press release, it warned: "Owners should stop using the products immediately. Contact the distributor you purchased from to request redress"

Brits waste money by spending too long in the shower.
Experts say there is a simple way for Brits to cut their energy bills - by taking shorter showers.
While some people may prefer to take their time in the morning and soak under the water as they wake up, getting in and out quickly helps to keep costs down.
The average UK shower lasts eight minutes. By cutting this by just two minutes, larger families could save around £50 during the summer, experts say.

This is based on a family of four using an electric shower during June, July and August.
Energy experts at Trade Radiators said taking six-minute showers instead could save £45.76 based on typical costs.
With many families still struggling with the cost of living, Brits are always searching for ways to keep costs down and save cash.
And this could be one easy way to do it.

It comes as energy prices remain high for millions of households following latest increases at the start of April.
Nicholas Auckland, from the firm, said: "Many people associate energy saving efforts with winter heating, but our data clearly shows that small adjustments to daily habits, even in summer, can lead to financial benefits.
“Cutting just two minutes from your shower is an easy win for both your wallet and the environment, and means that households can put that money towards good use rather than it washing away down the drain”.

Brian Wilson, co-​creator of iconic 1960s band The Beach Boys, dies aged 82
2 hours ago
Ali Abbas Ahmadi
BBC News, Toronto
Interview from 2011: How music takes Brian Wilson back to the 1960s
Brian Wilson, the legendary frontman and co-founder of The Beach Boys, has died at the age of 82, his family has announced.
"We are heartbroken to announce that our beloved father Brian Wilson has passed away," his family said in a statement shared online. "We are at a loss for words right now.
"Please respect our privacy at this time as our family [is] grieving. We realise that we are sharing our grief with the world."
Born in 1942 and raised in Hawthorne, California, Wilson formed a group with his younger brothers Carl and Dennis, cousin Mike Love and friend Al Jardine.
They went on to become one of the country's biggest rock bands, The Beach Boys.
One of the most commercially successful bands of all time, they have sold more than 100 million records globally, according to the group's website.
Brian Wilson obituary: Troubled genius who wrote most of The Beach Boys' hits
Music magazine Rolling Stone ranked them at 12 on its list of the "100 Greatest Artists of All Time".
Wilson churned out dozens of hit singles, including the three number one songs I Get Around, Help Me, Rhonda and Good Vibrations.
He was known for using the recording studio to create unique sounds, especially on the album Pet Sounds, which contributed to his reputation as a music pioneer.
Tributes have been pouring in for the beloved musician.
Frank Sinatra's daughter, Nancy Sinatra, who enjoyed a high-profile music career around the time of The Beach Boys' heyday, shared a picture with Brian Wilson on Instagram.
"His cherished music will live forever as he travels through the Universe and beyond," she wrote. "God bless you, sweet Brian."
Mick Fleetwood, of the band Fleetwood Mac, wrote: "Anyone with a musical bone in their body must be grateful for Brian Wilson's genius magical touch !! And greatly saddened of this major worldly loss!!"
Sean Ono Lennon, son of Beatles frontman John Lennon and Yoko Ono, called Wilson the "American Mozart" and a "one of a kind genius from another world".
"Anyone who really knows me knows how heartbroken I am about Brian Wilson passing," he wrote on X.
"Not many people influenced me as much as he did. I feel very lucky that I was able to meet him and spend some time with him. He was always very kind and generous."
Elton John called him a "true giant", while Rolling Stones guitarist Ronnie Wood said his "world is in mourning", as he noted that
Sly Stone
and Wilson both died this week.
Universal Music Group's chief executive Sir Lucian Grainge called Wilson "one of the most talented singer-songwriters in the history of recorded music".
"If there was a human being who made art out of inexpressible sadness it was Brian Wilson," the musician Questlove wrote in a long tribute on Instagram.
Micky Dolenz, the last surviving member of the band the Monkees, wrote of Wilson's passing "his melodies shaped a generation, his harmonies changed the game, and his soul came through in every note".
In a post on X, American singer-songwriter Tom Petty compared Wilson to Beethoven, writing "I don't think there's anything better than that."
Wilson lost his wife Melinda in 2024. The couple had been married for 24 years, and adopted their children Dakota Rose, Daria Rose, Delanie Rose, Dylan and Dash together.
Wilson also had two daughters, Carnie and Wendy, from his first marriage.
The musician was diagnosed as a paranoid schizophrenic in 1984, according to Forbes, when doctors found evidence that his use of psychedelic drugs had potentially damaged his brain.
In February 2024 it was revealed he had dementia.

Waiting to be voted out: Inside the confusion and chaos of Santa Cruz County’s health care layoffs
by
Christopher Neely
2 hours ago
June 11, 2025
Share this:
Click to email a link to a friend (Opens in new window)
Email
Click to share on X (Opens in new window)
X
Click to share on Facebook (Opens in new window)
Facebook
Click to share on Nextdoor (Opens in new window)
Nextdoor
Quick Take
For some Santa Cruz County health care workers facing layoffs, the long wait for a final budget decision felt like a slow unraveling, leaving dedicated government employees in a state of helplessness and anxious anticipation.
The temperature on the fifth floor of Santa Cruz County’s government building was comfortable Tuesday morning, but Diane Dymesich was feeling the heat as she nervously paced the hallway outside of the bustling board of supervisors chambers.
Dymesich, who just turned 57 and bubbles with a heart-on-her-sleeve energy, has worked as a phlebotomist at the Santa Cruz Health Center for 21 years, drawing blood samples from the county’s sickest, poorest, and highest
–
risk residents. But she was unsure whether she’d have a job come July 1. Her employment, and her long-held plans for retirement, now came down to a majority decision by five elected county lawmakers sitting behind the chamber dais, who would soon vote on whether to approve health department cuts and lay off nearly 12 full-time employees — Dymesich among them.
MORE local COVERAGE
Most health agency layoffs delayed after county lawmakers eke out budget compromise
For one’s employment to come down to board vote sounds more like the experience of a Wall Street executive than a middle-class government health care worker. Yet, that was the scene for Dymesich and her colleagues on Tuesday, and all they could do was watch.
“For me, it’s really hard, because this isn’t about my job performance, or my merit, or anything that I’ve had control over,” Dymesich said, fanning herself with the day’s agenda packet as she watched the
five supervisors
debate the budget. “These people don’t know my life, don’t know my story, don’t know anything about me but are making these decisions about my entire life going forward. I had a plan for my retirement, but now, I don’t know.”
Dymesich then turned to her colleague, Jeff Zajac, who stood silently preparing his thoughts for the public comment portion of the day’s meeting. Zajac has more than 20 years of experience as a phlebotomist, but joined the county lab only eight years ago. Now in his early 60s, he works as a senior assistant, supervising Dymesich and the other four full-time employees between the Watsonville and Santa Cruz health centers.
Zajac looked up over his reading glasses with a heavy, exhausted stare, gripping a maroon folder that matched the color of his long-sleeved shirt. He had not slept nor eaten the night before. He began drafting his public comments at 4:30 a.m., in a fit of restlessness, after he realized Tuesday likely marked the last time he could speak up to the people responsible for deciding this aspect of his and his coworkers’ fates.
MORE LOCAL COVERAGE
Santa Cruz County education leaders ‘fearful’ that Medicaid cuts may hurt mental health, special education
“I just turned 62, so starting a new job is very scary,” Zajac said. “At the beginning of last night, I was feeling pretty hopeless and numb, and a lot of disappointment in what’s happening.”
Dymesich, Zajac and their coworkers had known for more than a month that this past Tuesday would be decision day. In late April, the county’s
since-departed health services agency director
, Mónica Morales, announced her
proposal to lay off about 12 people
and close the county’s blood lab and radiology services as a way to mitigate a growing fiscal crisis within the health department. Staff have said the county’s health agency has had long-simmering structural issues — exacerbated by growing uncertainty around the state and federal dollars — and needed to be “right-sized.”
As Zajac and Dymesich stood at the back of the chambers and watched
interim Health Services Agency Director Jennifer Herrera
struggle to explain to Supervisor Manu Koenig why her department couldn’t offer any alternatives to the layoffs and lab closures, they were joined by another health care worker awaiting their fate: Fadi Ayyad, the chief radiologic technologist at the Santa Cruz Health Center’s radiology services. Ayyad, 38, arrived in beige medical scrubs, a scruffy beard and close-cropped black hair. Like Zajac, he hardly slept the night before, and called the past month-and-a-half wait for Tuesday’s budget vote “devastating.”
“It was pretty stressful yesterday just knowing that today is the day,” Ayyad said. “I had no appetite. I didn’t eat dinner, I didn’t eat breakfast today. It’s taken a mental toll on me because it’s not like I did anything wrong. I’ll be driving around, all happy, and then suddenly I will realize that, oh s–t, I’m about to lose my income.”
Ayyad has worked in county radiology for six years and can talk long and passionately about how X-rays, which he calls “the backbone of health care” and the picture worth a thousand words for doctors. He called working for the county “my dream job,” a feeling buttressed by the stability and benefits of government service. Ayyad’s long plan to retire as a Santa Cruz County employee was now flipped upside down.
“I had faith in this,” Ayyad told Lookout. “When I got this job, I was ready to be committed to this. This was
the
job. You just never think they would get rid of services.”
As Ayyad took a seat, the heat inside the chambers was rising as the supervisors continued what felt like a cross-examination of
Health Service Agency
executives and managers. The lawmakers criticized HSA for failing to bring alternatives to the layoffs despite multiple requests, and for failing to show their work, which left the elected officials with many unanswered questions as they prepared to vote.
“I think it would be helpful for us and the community if this was a little bit more transparent,” Koenig said. “I understand some of the other solutions you looked at were not as good, but nevertheless, there must have been multiple options weighed and I think that’s sort of the question mark that is lingering in the air and doesn’t seem answered.”
County Personnel Director Ajita Patel told the supervisors her team had been working with each of the employees who would be laid off, trying to find them placement within the county. She said some had chosen to retire, while she expected others to receive a county job offer by Friday.
“There are a couple who only want to seek placement at equal pay, and that is a little challenging because we don’t have a lot of vacancies at that level,” Patel said.
Late last week, County Executive Officer Carlos Palacios
proposed extending the blood lab
for another three months as it became clear the health department was not ready to make a smooth transition to private providers. As the supervisors discussed this option, it only exacerbated Dymesich and Zajac’s confusion about their future. They and their coworkers had already begun applying for other jobs within the county. What were they supposed to do now if they got one?
MORE LOCAL COVERAGE
‘No Kings’ and Juneteenth: Santa Cruz County’s eventful Saturday
“Look, I don’t know man, at this point I just need them to make a decision so I can move on and make decisions about the rest of my life,” Dymesich said.
Dymesich described the past several weeks as a sort of “Hunger Games” scenario among her coworkers. Those seeking work are prioritizing jobs within the county so they can continue building their pension and retirement plans. However, all of the county jobs, Dymesich and Zajac said, are demotions that come with pay cuts, and all of the coworkers are competing against one another for the positions.
Dymesich said she is in the final stages of accepting a job with a 31% pay decrease just so she can keep her county benefits for the next eight years before retirement.
“The hiring officer will probably call me asking for a reference for Diane because I’m her supervisor,” Zajac said, with Dymesich at his side. “But we’re going for the same job. And it’s like, ‘Yeah, Diane’s great, but I’m better.’”
Later in the day, hours after Zajac, Dymesich and Ayyad returned to work at the Santa Cruz Health Center, the board of
supervisors unanimously voted to approve
the Health Services Agency budget, but extend the blood lab and radiology services through September. As part of the extension, supervisors said they wanted the county’s health executives to work with front-line staff involved with lab and radiology to come up with some alternative options to shutting down the services.
Over the phone, Dymesich called the extension “interesting” but said she’s unsure how the lab will stay open for another three months when she and much of the staff are in the process of getting other jobs.
“It’s kind of too late, isn’t it? Because if any of us get a job, we have to take it,” Dymesich said. “None of these jobs are going to wait around for us to finish our lab role in three months. I feel a lot of loyalty to the lab, but we have to do what we have to do. It’s all around not a good situation for us. The whole thing just seems really sad.”
Zajac said he was hoping to have more closure but that Tuesday’s vote puts him and his coworkers in “an even tougher position,” in which they either take a more secure job and abandon their coworkers, or continue with uncertainty through the summer.
“If I find a good job I’m not going to put myself in this position of not knowing what’s going to happen for another three months,” Zajac said. “I’ve concluded that I need to take care of myself. I want to stay with the county. But there is a bad taste in my mouth as a consequence of what has happened over the last two months.”
Ayyad, on the other hand, plans to ride out the extension at the radiology center. He said
Watsonville Community Hospital
had reached out to him about a radiology position that he now planned to decline, or at least try to defer.
“A gray cloud is still over our heads regardless of the answer today, and that gray cloud was supposed to disappear,” Ayyad said. “I was ready to start applying and move on, but now it’s like we have another three months of this.”

A disturbing horror movie that's free to stream is so disturbing, viewers are reluctant to recommend it to others.
We're spoilt for choice when it comes to
streaming
services, with the likes of
Netflix
, Apple TV,
Amazon Prime
Video, Disney+ and more.
But one often over-looked option is Tubi, a free-to-use platform which doesn't even require sign-up for you to get streaming.
It happens to be home to a deranged
horror
movie apparently responsible for giving viewers 'hour-long anxiety attacks'.
Marketed as a 'black comedy', people reckon it's anything but - and blame the
film
for unlocking a new fear deep within them.
That's not stopped the movie from earning decent ratings though, especially for such a polarizing genre.
Viewers won't be forgetting the disturbing movie anytime soon (Apocalipsis Producciones)
I bet you're curious to know what it's all about...
Well, the story follows new parents Jesús and María (David Pareja and Estefanía de los Santos) who are struggling to adjust to life with a little one.
Adding to their stress is the purchase of a new coffee table. While seemingly minor, it turns out to be a major cause of contention between the couple.
On top of all this, Jesús is privately dealing with his neighbor's young daughter, who is bizarrely threatening to frame his as a pedophile.
Now, I don't want to go spoiling the entire movie here and to be honest, the less you know going in, the better.
So I'll just leave you with this: A seemingly ordinary day quickly descends into chaos in some gory and deeply disturbing ways.
The Coffee Table debuted in 2023 (Apocalipsis Producciones)
Anyway, over on
Reddit
, one user had made a bold request for 'insane' movies to watch.
"And I mean absolutely unhinged," they continued. "I don't mind it being humorous, I just want something that'll make me say 'what the f**k' at the end."
Among the outpouring of recommendations was the cryptically-named horror I'm talking about, named
The Coffee Table.
Reluctantly suggesting the movie, one
social media
user added: "Don't thank me later."
"Thought about suggesting that but felt too guilty in case they actually watched it," a second chipped in, warning: "Don't OP. I can't believe anyone would watch this more than once."
"I watched it last weekend and haven't stopped thinking about it since," a third admitted. "It's so well done, imo."
Be warned: the below trailer is pretty graphic in places - especially if you're squeamish. Don't watch it while eating, either.
﻿
﻿
Over on
Rotten Tomatoes
,
The Coffee Table
was awarded a pretty high score of 88 percent from critics, across 33 reviews.
Audience members, meanwhile, scored it 73 percent over more than 100 ratings.
"Years ago I went down a rabbit hole looking for the most brutal film I could find to see if I could tolerate it," one viewer wrote. "It’s too bad at the time
The Coffee Table
had not been made yet."
Another claimed the movie gave them a '60 minute long anxiety attack', and, describing the themes of the story, admitted: "This is a whole new level. New fear unlocked. Would not recommend this to anyone..."
Someone else weighed in: "It’s not even really horror, but very horrific. More of an intense drama and boy, this one is INTENSE. Worth a watch."
Another simply summed it up as an 'anxiety inducing nightmare', which is pretty accurate.
The Coffee Table
is available to stream for free via Tubi in the US, or with an Amazon Prime subscription in the UK. If you dare...

The rise in non-prescribed ketamine use across the UK in recent years is a cause for concern, say doctors in
The BMJ
.
Irene Guerrini at South London & Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust and colleagues warn that its low cost has made it popular among young people. They say public awareness of the risks and long-term harms associated with
ketamine
remains insufficient, and they call for better diagnostic criteria, a national registry, and screening tools to support earlier identification, guide treatment, and help evaluate emerging therapies.
Ketamine is routinely used as a general anesthetic and lower doses are prescribed for
chronic pain
,
treatment-resistant depression
and suicidality, they explain. Intranasal esketamine is also licensed for the treatment of depression.
But ketamine is also increasingly used recreationally at doses much higher than those prescribed for depression, which can cause serious health problems, such as irreversible damage to the bladder and kidneys and psychiatric conditions, they warn.
And as ketamine use increases, more individuals are seeking treatment for addiction. The number of people starting treatment for ketamine addiction in 2023-24 was 3,609, more than eight times higher than the 426 reported in 2014-15.
However, the authors point out that ketamine use disorders remain inadequately defined in psychiatric guidelines, and there is a lack of evidence around potential drugs for treatment and prevention.
Individuals who use ketamine also report that health services often lack an understanding of ketamine
addiction
and offer minimal treatment options specific to the drug, meaning treatment is often partially effective.
Balancing ketamine's medical value with rising non-prescribed use presents a complex challenge, write the authors.
"The Home Office is considering reclassifying ketamine as class A, but opinions remain divided. A proportionate response should go beyond legislation to include clear governance of therapeutic use, investment in treatment and prevention, and balanced public messaging."

content: Change is a constant in the technology world, and nowhere is this more evident than in the evolution of digital communities centered around major platforms like Windows and Microsoft's broader ecosystem. Long-time Windows Central editor Jez Corden recently penned a heartfelt reflection on this journey, spotlighting not only the dynamic environment facing enthusiast communities but also a series of tangible new features aimed at nurturing deeper connections among readers, contributors, and editorial staff. Despite surface-level transformations in branding, focus, and even ownership, Corden's message makes clear that the underlying mission of Windows Central—delivering authoritative news, reviews, and community engagement for Microsoft fans—remains resolute. With new technical infrastructure falling into place, 2025 finds the site re-emphasizing interactive features, inviting feedback, and looking to shape the next chapter alongside its audience. This article explores those shifts, critically examines the strengths and risks of the new direction, and places these developments in the broader context of today's tech media landscape. From Phone Fans to Ecosystem Architects​ When Corden joined Windows Central (then WPCentral) a decade ago, the editorial focus revolved around Windows Phone—an ill-fated but passionately supported line of mobile devices that, at its peak, nurtured one of the most loyal communities in the technology sphere. As Microsoft's ambitions changed, so too did the site's scope: first expanding to Xbox, Surface, and eventually every element of Microsoft's sprawling product lineup, including enterprise software and cloud infrastructure. In recent years, Microsoft's headlong push into artificial intelligence, cloud-based services, and its multi-platform strategies for Xbox have prompted further shifts in the site's editorial priorities. The sunsetting of Windows Phone is a cautionary tale about the impermanence of even the most vibrant consumer tech subcultures. Yet, as Windows Central has matured alongside its subject matter, the site has not only retained but, in some respects, deepened its engagement with a core audience that spans casual users, enterprise IT professionals, and gamers alike. According to Corden, fostering that sense of community has always been central to the site's DNA, even as the composition and interests of its readership have evolved. Why Community Features Matter More Than Ever​ At a time when social media platforms dominate online engagement, dedicated tech communities like Windows Central play a unique and increasingly vital role. Unlike transient conversations on Twitter or the noisy, algorithm-driven chaos of Reddit, these communities offer highly specialized forums for technical discussion, troubleshooting, sharing knowledge, and sometimes spirited debate over the merits of Windows updates, Xbox hardware refreshes, or the best way to wrangle Azure's ever-expanding feature set. But the frictionless, responsive, and often personalized experiences users have come to expect from internet platforms set a high bar. For tech sites, robust community features are no longer a luxury—they are existential. They drive both return visits and deeper site engagement, fueling a virtuous feedback loop between editorial content and grassroots discussion. In this context, Corden’s announcement of new community tools is both a return to form and a strategic imperative. The recent Future PLC acquisition brought significant changes, including a temporary loss of the site's custom comments system, which long served as an anchor for discussion and debate. The hiatus reportedly lasted about two years—a significant absence in digital terms—but the reintroduction comes with modern features and an explicit call for user input on what comes next. What’s New: The Revamped Commenting System​ So, what’s different this time around? The core upgrade is a new commenting engine, which Corden formally introduced despite it already being active for a while. Key features include: Unified Sign-In: Users can log in or create accounts using their existing forum credentials, allowing for seamless integration between article discussions and broader forum activity. Accessibility is emphasized, with a “Sign In” banner offering an instant way to participate. Centralized Comments Feed: Unlike earlier iterations, replies and threads can be tracked and engaged with from any page on the site, simplifying participation and keeping conversations visible to all. Auto-Moderation: The new system employs more assertive content filtering, with automated systems detecting and greenlighting comments—although Corden concedes these filters may be temporarily “over-aggressive.” This reflects a balancing act between fostering open discussion and preventing spam or hostility, a perpetual challenge for any tech community. Polls and Featured Comments: Editors can now elevate insightful responses and crowdsource opinions directly within discussion threads, hinting at interactive content and reader-driven editorial planning. Looking ahead, the editorial team hints at further expansions: custom badges, avatars, and other identity tools to foster user recognition and longer-term engagement. No exact timeline is specified, but the direction is clear—a return to the site’s community-driven roots, augmented by current-generation technical capability. Transparency, Limitations, and Honest Reflections​ Corden’s editorial stance stands out for its candor. He doesn’t attempt to gloss over the practical limitations involved—chief among them, staffing. The days of frequent, high-production video content (once led by Mark Guim, whom Corden acknowledges with nostalgia) are over, at least for now. Likewise, experimental ventures like the community Discord proved too resource-intensive to moderate and actively maintain. This honesty about resource constraints is refreshing in an era where many tech publications mask logistical realities behind a veneer of unbounded ambition. By explicitly stating what is—and isn’t—possible with current tools and staff levels, Windows Central signals a genuine commitment to sustainable community management. It’s an approach that’s likely to engender more understanding among dedicated users and reduce the cycle of over-promising and under-delivering that plagues some digital media efforts. Editorial Direction and User Agency​ A distinguishing feature of the new approach is the explicit invitation for user feedback—not just in the abstract, but as a guiding force for upcoming features, editorial focus, and community culture. Corden asks directly: What do you want to see more of? Whether it’s contests, giveaways, discussion threads, or new content verticals, the editorial team positions itself as a partner rather than a gatekeeper. Such moves are more than marketing gestures. In digital publishing, a participatory editorial model is increasingly proven to support site longevity. Sites that fail to adapt to audience interests risk not only stagnation but outright irrelevance. By collecting and collating feedback for use in future planning, Windows Central opens itself to course corrections that reflect shifting community needs—an agility that, if properly implemented, could serve as a valuable differentiator. Risks and Points for Caution​ Despite these positive steps, several challenges and potential pitfalls remain: Technical teething issues: Early reports confirm that the new auto-moderation tools are sometimes too restrictive, potentially stifling legitimate debate. The team’s promise to “greenlight” innocuous comments caught by filters is encouraging, but overzealous moderation can chill engagement if not rapidly improved. Fragmentation risk: The pivot away from platforms like Discord, along with the challenge of integrating forums, comment threads, and editorial content, runs the risk of fragmenting community discussion across different silos. Unified identity and notification tools are a good start, but ongoing investment in cross-platform functionality will be essential. Resource dependency: As Corden acknowledges, some community-building initiatives require more staff time and creative bandwidth than are currently available. Without a clear roadmap—particularly for labor-intensive features like custom video, live chats, or real-time moderation—ambitious plans might stall or backfire. Ownership and oversight: With parent company Future PLC in charge, some aspects of site management may be subject to external influence or delayed by broader corporate priorities. History shows that platform acquisitions often introduce uncertainty, whether through sudden changes in policy or protracted development timelines for desired features. Comparative Analysis: How Does Windows Central Stack Up?​ To understand the impact and prospects of these changes, it’s worth situating Windows Central within the broader tech community ecosystem. Major competitors like The Verge, Tom’s Hardware, and Ars Technica all offer some combination of custom comment engines, reader Q&As, and sometimes forum extensions. Each faces similar hurdles—automated moderation quality, spam prevention, and sustaining lively (but civil) conversation. Notably, many large sites have chosen to deprecate or even remove comments entirely in recent years, citing the cost of moderation and abuse risk. Wired, for instance, shut down its comment section in 2022 and relies mainly on social media for engagement. In contrast, Windows Central’s renewed investment in on-site commenting places it among a minority of publications betting that strong in-house community features deliver more long-term value than outsourcing discussion to Twitter/X or Facebook. This strategy brings both opportunities and risks. A thriving on-site community can provide direct editorial feedback, keep pageviews high, and strengthen brand loyalty—especially important in an era when third-party traffic sources are increasingly volatile. At the same time, it demands continuous moderation and technical improvement, with little margin for error if hostile actors attempt to disrupt the space. Opportunities: Leveraging New Community Tools​ Handled deftly, the new commenting system could do more than just restore previous levels of engagement—it could catalyze new forms of reader interaction: Editorial polling and crowdsourcing: Built-in polls can inform content decisions, helping editors target topics that matter most to their core audience. This can make editorial output both more responsive and resilient to shifts in Microsoft’s own strategy cycles. Featured comments and contributor highlights: By elevating particularly insightful or expert commentary, Windows Central can blur the line between reader and contributor, fostering a culture of learned discourse reminiscent of the best technical forums. Feedback loops for feature development: As the development of custom badges and avatars proceeds, early user feedback can be incorporated quickly. This approach mirrors “agile” development best practices widely used in the software industry and, if executed transparently, could establish the site as a paragon of responsive community management. Event-driven engagement: While staffing currently limits higher-touch efforts like live streams or video Q&As, occasional contests or giveaways can stoke periodic surges of participation. If tracked and analyzed, these surges may provide invaluable data on what motivates readers most deeply. The Path Forward: Building for the Next Ten Years​ Ultimately, the relaunch of Windows Central’s commenting and community features is both a nod to the past and a vote of confidence in the continued relevance of specialist tech publishing. The Microsoft ecosystem—once defined by desktop operating systems and proprietary hardware—is now a bewildering array of cloud services, AI models, gaming platforms, and edge devices. The role of an enthusiast site is to help users make sense of this sprawl, while also giving them a place to celebrate, critique, and influence the technology shaping their lives. Corden’s open letter, and the responsive strategy it introduces, points toward a more collaborative future—one that recognizes community insight not as an afterthought, but as a core pillar of editorial growth and site development. If Windows Central can iterate quickly, ease moderation pain-points, and sustain editorial transparency in the face of external pressures, it could set a model for the next generation of enthusiast communities. Conclusion: An Open Call—and a Lesson for Tech Media​ The ongoing revitalization of Windows Central’s community features highlights both the opportunities and the complexities faced by modern tech media. Where once lively discussion boards were (almost) taken for granted, today’s highly fragmented, increasingly competitive environment means cultivating a healthy on-site community is harder—but also more necessary—than ever. The site’s willingness to acknowledge limitations, invite honest feedback, and iterate publicly offers a valuable blueprint for peers and competitors. Success will depend on finding the right balance between automation and human judgment, ambition and realism, tradition and innovation. In the end, the real asset of any tech publication isn’t just its news scoops or hot takes—it’s the people who show up, day after day, to build something together. Windows Central’s message is clear: the door is open, the comment section is back, and the next chapter depends on you. For readers, contributors, and tech enthusiasts alike, the invitation couldn’t come at a more critical or exciting time. content: As the Windows 10 era draws to a close, millions of users are confronted with a critical dilemma: how to operate safely when official security updates from Microsoft come to an end. The cessation of updates, scheduled for October 14, 2025, doesn’t mean Windows 10 machines will instantly become obsolete, but it does expose them to escalating risks, especially from online threats that target unpatched vulnerabilities. This comprehensive feature explores the practical steps, inherent risks, and nuanced decisions that users and organizations must weigh as the operating system transitions to end-of-life status. The End of Windows 10 Security Updates: What’s at Stake?​ Microsoft’s decision to stop releasing security patches, bug fixes, and technical support for Windows 10 is not unprecedented. The company has adhered to a similar lifecycle model for previous versions, including Windows 7 and XP before it. However, with an estimated one billion Windows 10 installations as recently as early 2023, the scale and urgency of this transition are significant. Cybercriminals actively seek vulnerabilities in unsupported operating systems. Once an official end-of-support date is reached, these systems are prime targets. The stakes are higher for any devices processing sensitive data, operating in regulated industries, or exposed to the internet through daily use. Impact on Regular Users and Organizations​ For home users, the most immediate consequence is an increased risk from malware, phishing, ransomware, and other digital threats. The majority of attacks exploit known vulnerabilities, and once Microsoft stops patching Windows 10, these vulnerabilities remain open indefinitely. Businesses face even greater risk, especially if compliance with laws like GDPR, HIPAA, or PCI DSS is required. Many of these regulations compel the use of supported, actively patched software. Continuing to run Windows 10 without official updates could have legal, financial, and reputational ramifications. Your Options After End-of-Support​ Microsoft and the broader tech community present several pathways for users facing Windows 10’s end of life. Each comes with its own blend of benefits, challenges, and risks. Upgrade to Windows 11: The Official Route​ For most, transitioning to Windows 11 is the straightforward solution. This operating system, launched in late 2021, delivers key improvements in security (in part due to enhanced hardware requirements), user interface design, and performance. If your PC passes Microsoft’s compatibility checks—which include requirements like TPM 2.0 and recent-generation CPUs—the upgrade process is generally smooth, with a free license for Windows 11 available for genuine Windows 10 installations. Before upgrading: Back up essential data . Although the upgrade is designed to be seamless, failures can occur, especially on aging drives. Plug in your laptop . Interruptions from power loss during the upgrade can corrupt the operating system installation. Allocate time for setup and updates . The upgrade, subsequent updates, and post-installation tweaks may take several hours. Check peripheral compatibility . Ensure your printers, scanners, and other accessories have Windows 11-compatible drivers. Benefits of the Official Upgrade​ Upgrading brings continuing security updates, new features, and technical support from Microsoft. Windows 11’s hardware requirements, while controversial, do offer significant security enhancements, including: Secure Boot and TPM 2.0, making it much harder for malware to gain low-level system access. Improved memory protection and virtualization-based security. Ongoing integration with Microsoft Defender and cloud-based identity safeguards. These features collectively reduce your exposure to modern attack methods. Compatibility Limitations​ Many PCs, especially those launched before 2018, fail the Windows 11 hardware checks. Microsoft stands by these requirements, asserting that older processors and missing TPM chips pose unacceptable security risks. Replace Your Computer: The Most Secure Long-Term Strategy​ If your device fails to meet Windows 11’s requirements, especially if it’s over five years old, replacement is the most prudent option. New computers come pre-installed with Windows 11 and offer tangible day-to-day improvements: Faster performance and energy efficiency. Sharper displays and better video calling hardware. Latest Wi-Fi and Bluetooth standards. Newer ports for more seamless connections to external devices. Enhanced cooling and battery lifespan. While the expense of a new system isn’t trivial, the investment is offset by improved productivity, greater reliability, and vastly reduced risk of cyberattack. Unofficial Windows 11 Workarounds: A Risky Middle Ground​ For technically savvy users, unofficial methods to circumvent Windows 11’s strict hardware requirements exist. These involve registry edits or third-party tools that disable compatibility checks, allowing “unsupported” upgrades. Microsoft’s Position​ Microsoft has published guidance for IT professionals on installing Windows 11 on unsupported hardware, but does not recommend it for everyday users. Key caveats include: No guarantee of future updates . Security and feature updates may be withheld. Possible instability . Unsupported systems might encounter bugs or crashes. Limited or missing driver support . New devices and peripherals may not work. No official technical support . If things go wrong, you’re on your own. When (and Why) to Consider It​ This approach may buy some time for users who understand and can manage the risks. However, it’s not a sustainable long-term solution, as future feature or security updates may fail, or extended Windows 11 updates could become unavailable for such machines. Extended Security Updates (ESUs): Paying for Extra Time​ This option, introduced with Windows 7’s sunset, enables organizations—and potentially individual consumers—to pay for continued critical security updates for a defined period. Microsoft plans to offer ESUs for Windows 10, focusing initially on business and educational customers, though expanded access for individual users remains uncertain. ESU Caveats​ Not free . ESUs are usually priced per device and can become expensive over time. Limited scope . Only critical security vulnerabilities are patched. Eventual end . ESUs have a fixed end date—typically two to three years. For large organizations managing legacy applications or devices, ESUs are a lifeline during the transition period. For average users, it’s a stop-gap at best. Strengths of Windows 10’s End-of-Life Strategies​ Despite the perceived inconvenience, Microsoft’s phased approach to ending Windows 10 support adheres to security best practices. The clear communication about end-of-support and upgrade options gives users time to plan. Notable advantages include: Improved overall ecosystem security . Encouraging users to upgrade or replace hardware closes persistent attack vectors, making widespread malware outbreaks less likely. Clear upgrade paths . Users with newer hardware benefit from free, officially supported upgrades. ESUs offer transition time for businesses with complex requirements. Risks and Weaknesses​ However, unavoidable downsides and dangers persist: Massive numbers of unpatched systems . Historical precedent shows that millions of machines will remain unpatched long after official support ends, creating fertile ground for cybercriminals. Attacks like WannaCry and NotPetya—both exploiting vulnerabilities in unsupported systems—underscore the risks. Cost barriers . Many users cannot immediately afford new hardware, making them more likely to continue using increasingly vulnerable systems. Workarounds can backfire . Unsupported upgrades may appear to solve the problem, but users could soon find themselves locked out of critical updates or facing inexplicable system failures. Privacy and compliance . For businesses, running unsupported OSes can lead to serious breaches of data protection regulations. Mitigation and Hardening for Those Staying on Windows 10​ For users and organizations unable to upgrade by October 2025, several steps can enhance safety, though none fully compensate for the lack of security updates. Best Practices if You Must Stay​ Isolate critical systems . Disconnect unsupported machines from the internet wherever possible. Use them only for offline tasks to eliminate remote attack vectors. Deploy strong endpoint protection . Leading antivirus vendors often release updates for unsupported Windows versions for several years. However, this is not a panacea—antivirus can’t patch operating system holes. Apply latest updates before the deadline . Make sure all official patches are installed before October 14, 2025. Limit permissions . Restrict user accounts to standard privileges rather than administrator, minimizing the risk of malware gaining system-wide control. Use modern browsers and applications . Third-party vendors like Google and Mozilla typically support Windows 10 for some time post-EOL, but eventually, updates will stop. Monitor network activity . Use firewalls and intrusion prevention systems to track unusual activity. Back up regularly . Maintain offline and cloud backups of critical files to mitigate ransomware or data loss incidents. Educate users . Most breaches begin with social engineering; updated awareness training remains essential. Consider Linux as a Lifeline​ For older PCs incapable of running Windows 11, replacing Windows with a lightweight Linux distribution is a compelling alternative. Linux Mint, Ubuntu, and similar distros run efficiently on aging hardware, offer modern security updates, and feature familiar interfaces. While the learning curve can be steep, most common tasks—web browsing, office productivity, and media playback—are well supported. Key caveats: Application compatibility for Windows-specific software may require workarounds like Wine. Peripheral support varies, but has improved dramatically in recent years. Looking Beyond 2025: Long-Term Security Trends​ The end-of-life transition for Windows 10 reflects recurring challenges in the technology landscape: balancing innovation with legacy support, guiding users through change without exposing them to undue risk. Microsoft’s shift towards hardware-rooted security in Windows 11 marks a new chapter, raising the bar for baseline protections, but also highlighting a growing divide between current and legacy systems. As extended security updates become mainstream, and with initiatives like Microsoft’s Windows 365 cloud PC emerging, it’s clear that the definition of a “supported device” is evolving. The overarching trend is towards managed, always-updated, cloud-integrated devices, but millions will continue to depend on traditional Windows PCs for years. The Real-World Bottom Line​ Running an unsupported Windows 10 machine past the cut-off is like driving a car without airbags or seat belts: it may keep rolling, but the risks escalate with each passing month. The best time to plan your migration is now, not on the eve of the deadline. For most, upgrading to Windows 11 or investing in a modern device is the safest, most reliable path forward. For the technically adept, applying unofficial workarounds can delay—but not solve—the inevitability of change. And for businesses, budgeting for ESUs may provide necessary breathing room to transition critical systems. Regardless of your approach, proactive planning, layered security protections, and continual awareness will be your best allies as Windows 10 moves into history. As always, the weakest link isn’t technological, but human: the decision not to act until it's too late. By understanding the stakes and preparing accordingly, Windows 10 users can bridge the gap to a more secure, modern computing future—on their own terms. Octopus Energy sending 'little gadget' to UK households which can help slash bills
25,000 Octopus customers will receive the device in June
Comments
News
Christian Abbott
Audience Writer
08:32, 12 Jun 2025
(Image: PA)
Octopus Energy has launched a new product that it is sending out to customers' homes in a bid to get the most accurate energy data to help them control it effortlessly.
This is the Octopus Home Mini, and 200,000 homes across the UK are already using the device that the energy provider calls "sustainable, smart, and totally free for Octopus customers."
‌
As stated on Octopus's website, the product was first launched just 2 years ago to "give people easy access to their real-time energy data and help them take control of how and when they use electricity.
‌
Read more:
UK households warned over 'rarest' 1p coin worth up to £200,000 which could 'change your life'
"It connects directly to your smart meter and, through the Octopus app, gives you a clear, up-to-the-minute view of how much energy your home is using (and which gadgets are guzzling the most)."
This is a free product for Octopus customers that helps improve smart meter connections.
Article continues below
The Mini is essentially a range extender, making sure your meters talk to each other and the data keeps flowing.
To apply for an Octopus Home Mini, which remains in beta, you will need to fill out some details on the
energy supplier's website
to have a chance of getting one.
Once you receive the device, the step-up process is simple:
‌
Make sure you've got the latest version of the Octopus app and you're logged in.
Check your phone is connected to WiFi (you'll need a 2.4GHz WiFi network, it won't work with 5GHz), and Bluetooth is on.
Plug in your OHM at the wall using the plug and USB cable - you'll need to keep it plugged in even when you've set it up. It needs to be as close to your electricity meter as possible and within WiFi range.
Scan the QR code on the OHM (you can also find it in your mini setup booklet) or use this link:
octopus.energy/app/devices/setup-home-mini
. Both the QR code or the link will take you to the Octopus app where you'll be guided through the rest of the set up.
Your OHM has colourful LED lights to display its connection state. The light will flash blue, then it'll turn green and once it's fully connected, it'll turn white.
Derya, Lead Product Engineer said: "People keep telling us how easy it is to set up. They just plug it in, follow a few steps on the app, and they’re good to go.
"We’ve had some customers say it’s the quickest bit of tech they’ve ever set up."

content: Por TIM REYNOLDS INDIANÁPOLIS (AP) — Arriba por diez al final del tercer cuarto. En ventaja por siete al inicio del último periodo. Los Pacers tenían una oportunidad de oro. Y en un chasquido la perdieron.. Una oportunidad de tomar una ventaja de 3-1 en las Finales de la NBA se le escapó de las manos a Indiana el viernes por la noche, cuando el Thunder de Oklahoma City se impuso por 31-17 en el cuarto final para llevarse el triunfo 111-104 y empatar la serie a cuatro victorias por bando. Un cierre espectacular de Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, el Jugador Más Valioso de la NBA, fue clave para Oklahoma City. Así de rápido, la serie esá igualada de cara al quinto partido. “Es frustrante, por supuesto”, afirmó el guardia de los Pacers, Tyrese Haliburton. “Quieres ganar ese partido… pero no se dieron las cosas”. Un vistazo a cómo ocurrió la remontada — o el colapso, dependiendo de la perspectiva: Pacers 89, Thunder 82, 10:56 restantes Obi Toppin — quien acababa de hacer una gran clavada unos tres minutos antes para darle a Indiana su primera ventaja de diez puntos en la serie — tuvo otro mate, que frenó una tímida reacción del Thunder y restituyó una ventaja de siete puntos para los Pacers. Indiana se enfrió a partir de ahí, fallando 12 de sus últimos 16 tiros de campo. Los Pacers se doblaron pero no se rompieron El Thunder empató el encuentro a 89, a 91, a 95 y a 97. Y cada vez, los Pacers tenían una respuesta. Haliburton hizo una bandeja para que Indiana tomara una ventaja de 91-89 con 7:50 minutos restantes. Andrew Nembhard encestó un tiro para una ventaja de 93-91 con 6:59 minutos por jugar. Haliburton anotó de nuevo para colocar la delantera en 97-95 con 5:03 minutos restantes, y realizó un par de tiros libres con 4:19 por jugar para romper otro empate. “Tuvimos algunas jugadas desmoralizantes. Era fácil rendirse en un partido así”, comentó el entrenador del Thunder, Mark Daigneault. Su equipo — y el Jugador Más Valioso de la liga — hicieron lo contrario. SGA toma el control La ventaja de Indiana era de cuatro puntos con 3:20 minutos restantes, 103-99. Pero entró en acción el Jugador Más Valioso. Gilgeous-Alexander anotó ocho puntos en los siguientes tres minutos; los Pacers no consiguieron ninguno. Él solo decidió el resultado. “Las faltas fueron un problema”, expresó el entrenador de los Pacers, Rick Carlisle. “Mira, es un gran jugador. Ése es otro problema. Es el Jugador Más Valioso… Pero oye, estás arriba por siete en casa. Tienes que esforzarte y encontrar una manera, y no pudimos hacerlo esta noche”. ¿Y ahora qué? Indiana sabe que ahora tiene que ganar al menos un juego más en Oklahoma City para convertirse en monarca de la NBA. Los Pacers ganaron el primer partido allí; saben que es posible. “Estoy emocionado por el desafío”, manifestó Haliburton. _____ Deportes en español AP: https://apnews.com/hub/deportes Esta historia fue traducida del inglés por un editor de AP con la ayuda de una herramienta de inteligencia artificial generativa.

content: Matthew Snider, Chief Investment Officer at Digital Wealth Partners, has issued a cautionary statement to XRP retail investors following a significant development involving Trident Digital. The financial firm recently disclosed its plan to build a $500 million XRP reserve, a move that could impact the availability of XRP in the broader market. Trident Digital’s XRP Reserve Strategy Trident Digital, a Nasdaq-listed company, announced its intention to raise $500 million through a combination of stock offerings and financial instruments. The funds will be used to establish a substantial XRP treasury, with implementation scheduled to begin in the latter half of this year, pending regulatory clearance. At present, the firm is engaging with institutional investors and other stakeholders to determine the optimal approach for acquiring XRP and managing the reserve infrastructure. With this move, Trident joins the ranks of other publicly traded companies that have announced similar plans to hold XRP in their corporate treasuries. These companies include Webus International, Wellgistics Health, and VivoPower, among others. Implications for Retail Access to XRP In light of the growing institutional interest, Snider warned that the supply of XRP available for individual investors could face increasing constraints. He highlighted that sustained corporate accumulation could restrict the effectiveness of dollar-cost averaging (DCA) , a method in which investors buy an asset at regular intervals to reduce price volatility over time. Snider’s concern is rooted in the possibility that large-scale purchases by corporations might remove significant quantities of XRP from the circulating supply. If institutional reserves continue to grow, the availability of XRP on public exchanges may decline, limiting opportunities for everyday investors to accumulate the token steadily. We are on twitter, follow us to connect with us :- @TimesTabloid1 — TimesTabloid (@TimesTabloid1) July 15, 2023 While such a supply restriction could positively influence XRP’s price trajectory, Snider noted that retail participants may be priced out or unable to maintain consistent accumulation. His statement implies that investors considering XRP should act sooner rather than later, before institutional interest accelerates further. XRP Holding Benchmarks Remain Debated As the conversation around XRP adoption intensifies, discussions have also emerged regarding the ideal quantity of XRP to hold for long-term financial benefit. The XRP community remains divided on what constitutes a meaningful amount for personal investment. Edo Farina, founder of Alpha Lions Academy, suggests that holding at least 1,000 XRP could be a reasonable benchmark for retail investors aiming to benefit from future growth. In contrast, other voices in the community, such as King Vale, argue that a minimum of 50,000 XRP is necessary to achieve financial success. At current prices, that would require an investment of over $100,000, a threshold many consider unrealistic. This has led to criticism from some community members, including commentator Xena, who argues that such figures are arbitrary and often serve to inflate investor egos rather than offer practical guidance. According to critics, individual investment goals and risk tolerance should dictate how much XRP one holds, not broad community speculation. The announcement from Trident Digital marks another step in the growing trend of institutional involvement in XRP. As more corporations express interest in integrating the asset into their financial frameworks, retail investors may face new challenges in accessing XRP through traditional accumulation strategies. Snider’s warning underscores the urgency for those considering investment to reassess their plans before broader market dynamics shift further out of reach. Pensioner households with income of £70,000 to get payments worth up to £300
Millions more pensioners will get winter support this year
Comments
News
Richard Guttridge
Agenda Editor
08:31, 12 Jun 2025
Millions more pensioners will get Winter Fuel Payments.
Pensioner households with incomes of up to £70,000 will get winter support payments later this year.
The winter fuel allowance will be extended to millions more pensioners following eligibility changes confirmed by the Government.
‌
But a quirk of the system means an older couple could receive a joint income of £70,000 and qualify for Winter Fuel Payments, while a single person getting £36,000 would not.
‌
READ MORE:
Nationwide, Lloyds, NatWest and Santander customers can claim £500
Get our best money saving tips and hacks by signing up to our newsletter
That's because the new rules state individuals must have an income of £35,000 or less to qualify for the winter payments, worth up to £300.
Article continues below
This is the case whether the person lives on their own or with a partner.
Couples will both qualify if they individually have incomes of less than £35,000 - meaning the maximum is £70,000 per couple.
The new criteria has been confirmed as part of major changes for winter 2025/26 following a backlash over cuts last year.
‌
Around nine million pensioners will now get the allowance, up from just over a million last winter.
Every pensioner will initially receive the cash but it will be clawed back from those with incomes of over £35,000 through tax returns.
The payments are worth £300 for couples over 80, and £200 for those under 80.
Article continues below
Most eligible people normally receive them during November, and the cash should arrive before
Christmas
.
Chancellor Rachel Reeves said: "We have now acted to expand the eligibility of the Winter Fuel Payment so no pensioner on a lower income will miss out.
"This will mean over three quarters of pensioners receiving the payment in England and Wales later this winter.”

content: Enterprises seeking to balance the relentless pressure of IT cost optimization with the demands of high performance and security are finding a compelling ally in the combination of Snapdragon processors and Windows 11 devices. With technology refresh cycles under scrutiny and operational efficiency a top priority, understanding the economic and practical advantages of this pairing has never been more essential. Recent research, independent benchmarking, and evolving enterprise requirements suggest that Snapdragon-powered PCs running Windows 11 not only lower total cost of ownership and extend device lifespan but also deliver measurable boosts in user productivity and organizational agility. The Economic Impact of Windows 11: A Data-Driven Perspective​ A pivotal study conducted by Forrester in December 2022 established that organizations implementing Windows 11 devices on a four-year lifecycle can expect up to a 250% return on investment (ROI). For a company with 2,000 employees, this translates into substantial hard-dollar savings and operational improvements, validated by primary research and several detailed case studies. Importantly, these financial benefits stem from three main pillars: enhanced security, IT management efficiencies, and elevated user productivity. Enhanced Security: Lowering Risk and Cutting Costs​ Security remains a perennial concern, particularly in an era of advanced cyber threats and regulatory pressures. Windows 11, by default, leverages a hardware-backed security architecture, including TPM 2.0 chips, Secure Boot, and full-disk encryption via BitLocker. Advanced features like virtualization-based security (VBS) and hypervisor-protected code integrity (HVCI) add further resilience. According to Forrester’s assessment, Windows 11 reduces the risk of successful security breaches by 20% compared to prior versions. This reduction is due to both the robust baked-in OS protections and smoother integrations with third-party security tools, which together shrink the attack surface without introducing management complexity. These security gains further translate into tangible financial savings by decreasing security incidents and reducing the need for additional security solutions—an outcome that naturally appeals to IT departments tasked with squeezing the most value from every budgeted dollar. IT Management Efficiencies: Streamlining Operations​ Windows 11 brings a suite of improvements aimed at reducing the friction of day-to-day IT tasks. Automated provisioning, streamlined device enrollment, and easier management interfaces empower IT teams to deploy and maintain devices faster. Forrester’s findings show that organizations moving to Windows 11 realized: A 25% increase in deployment and provisioning efficiency A 20% lift in security team efficiency A remarkable reduction in help desk requests related to OS and device issues: 40% in the first year, 70% in the second, and 90% by the third year This cascade of efficiencies allows organizations to reallocate IT resources to more strategic initiatives, enhancing not only internal perceptions of IT value but also accelerating digital transformation agendas. End-User Productivity: Upgrading the Workforce​ End users see direct productivity benefits. Forrester quantifies a 15% average productivity boost for Windows 11 users, attributed in part to enhanced hardware (improved video, audio, and connectivity) and the streamlined, intuitive interface of the new operating system. In a distributed and hybrid work world, such gains—multiplied across thousands of employees—amount to significant competitive advantage. Snapdragon X Series: Supercharging the Windows 11 Value Proposition​ While Windows 11 lays out a solid foundation for productivity, security, and efficiency, the underlying hardware matters immensely—especially as computing shifts to more mobile, AI-centric, and energy-aware paradigms. Here, Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Series processors distinguish themselves. Power Management and Battery Life: Beyond the Status Quo​ Snapdragon X Elite and X Plus processors are engineered with power efficiency at the core. According to qualified benchmarking data (Geekbench v6.2 multi-thread and single-thread results on Windows 11 across credible reference designs): Snapdragon X Elite matches leading competitors' single-threaded CPU performance at 70% less power consumption. Snapdragon X Plus achieves multi-threaded parity at 54% less power. These claims are further supported by in-the-field tests, which indicate: Over 2x longer battery life during Microsoft Teams calls Up to 58% longer battery life for web browsing Up to 40% longer battery life for Office 365 apps Maximum device battery life approaching 22 hours per charge (manufacturer-quoted figures; actual results will vary based on specific usage and device configuration) Critically, this power efficiency not only extends single-charge endurance but reduces battery wear over time, translating to more charge cycles before battery performance degradation—a key consideration in keeping devices useful for a longer operational lifetime. Battery Longevity: Practical Advice for Enterprises​ Enterprises can further extend battery health by adopting best practices such as charging lithium-ion batteries to only 80%, instead of completely to 100%. This practice has been independently validated by battery research, and is now reflected in hardware management policies at innovative organizations. Hardware Longevity and AI-Ready Specifications​ As software evolves, so do hardware requirements—particularly in the age of on-device AI. Microsoft’s minimum specification for Copilot+ PCs is set at: 16GB RAM At least 40 neural processing unit (NPU) TOPS (trillions of operations per second) 256GB storage Every Snapdragon X Series-powered PC meets or exceeds these thresholds, ensuring they remain relevant and capable as enterprise applications integrate AI-driven workflows. ISVs such as Adobe, Zoom, Teams, Blender, Cephable, and Visual Studio Code are already rolling out on-device AI features that require hardware resources often lacking in legacy or economy-class devices. Device Performance Unplugged​ Traditional x86-based laptops typically exhibit a significant performance drop when disconnected from power (unplugged mode), often throttling CPU and GPU speeds to conserve battery. Independent testing (as cited in recent benchmark comparisons) indicates Snapdragon-powered Windows 11 devices are up to 90% faster than other leading processors when unplugged, providing users with responsive experiences regardless of location or proximity to a power outlet. Environmental and Sustainability Impacts​ Extending the useable life of PCs reduces both e-waste and the environmental footprint associated with frequent device replacement. Organizations attuned to sustainability mandates can leverage these benefits as concrete contributions toward net-zero and ESG reporting targets. However, realizing the full impact depends on disciplined device recycling and responsible disposal practices. Additional Cost Savings Layered Across the Stack​ Beyond the fundamental savings delivered through initial device acquisition, power efficiency, and extended hardware lifespan, Snapdragon Windows 11 devices offer secondary—and sometimes overlooked—cost advantages. Reduced Downtime and Workflow Interruptions​ Longer battery life translates directly into reduced downtime. Employees’ ability to work a full day without seeking a power outlet minimizes the frequency and duration of interruptions, supporting deeper focus and productivity—in line with flow state research widely cited in organizational psychology. Streamlined IT Infrastructure and Software Stack​ Migrating to Windows 11 not only delivers new capabilities but often enables organizations to sunset software solutions now duplicated or obviated by native OS features (e.g., remote desktop tools, encryption utilities, security add-ons). This software rationalization further lowers licensing, support, and management costs. Improved Productivity With AI Copilots​ Microsoft’s research indicates that 70% of Copilot for Microsoft 365 users report meaningful productivity improvements, while a controlled experiment found that developers using GitHub Copilot completed tasks up to 55.8% faster than those without access to the AI assistant. While such figures are impressive, it is important to note they are self-reported or derived from carefully controlled environments, so real-world impact may vary. Critical Analysis: Strengths and Caveats​ No analysis is complete without a clear-eyed look at limitations, implementation factors, and context. Strengths​ Holistic Security : Layered security spanning firmware, hardware, and software, coupled with Windows 11’s aggressive security model, significantly hardens the endpoint. Economic Efficiency : The ROI figures from respected, independent consultancies like Forrester are robust and corroborated across multiple case studies and industry settings. Workforce Enablement : The blend of battery life, unplugged performance, and AI-ready specifications positions Snapdragon Windows 11 devices as future-proof endpoints for a fast-evolving digital workplace. Sustainability : By facilitating longer refresh cycles, these devices contribute credibly to sustainability initiatives. Potential Risks and Limitations​ Compatibility Caveats : While Windows 11 for ARM (Snapdragon is ARM-based) has seen tremendous progress in app compatibility, a minority of legacy or specialized x86 applications may still encounter performance or functional limitations. Recent reports suggest a continually shrinking gap, but IT decision-makers must validate compatibility for business-critical workloads before wide-scale deployment. Battery Life Variability : Battery ratings are highly dependent on usage patterns, device configurations, and environmental factors. Real-world longevity is often harder to predict than lab benchmarks suggest. Organizations should pilot with a representative workload before scaling up. Pricing and Supply Chain : Initial unit costs for Snapdragon-powered business laptops can sometimes be higher than those for legacy x86 machines, offset over time by lower power and support costs. Supply chain issues—though diminished in 2025—can still introduce procurement delays for specific models. AI Workload Readiness : The usefulness of on-device AI accelerators (NPUs) depends on the adoption rate of compatible AI-enhanced software in the enterprise stack. While momentum is strong, lagging software support could delay the realization of full ROI on hardware AI capabilities. Verifying the Claims: Industry and Customer Context​ To critically assess claims, it’s essential to triangulate data points from independent sources: Forrester’s ROI Numbers : Various industry analyses, including IDC and Gartner, have corroborated elevated ROI and TCO benefits for organizations migrating to Windows 11, especially when combined with modern hardware. Battery and Performance Benchmarks : Numerous third-party reviews—including from PCWorld, Tom’s Hardware, and AnandTech—have published findings broadly in line with Qualcomm’s internal benchmarking, though occasionally noting underwhelming GPU or app emulation results in corner cases. Consistency is highest for mainstream productivity, communications, and collaboration workloads. AI Features Adoption : Early adopter feedback suggests tangible productivity gains from Copilot and similar AI-powered tooling, with caveats around data privacy, cost of licenses, and required training. Recommendations for IT Decision Makers​ Evaluate Before You Refresh​ Conduct a pilot program with representative user profiles and workloads prior to broad deployment. Measure not only headline battery life and performance but also app compatibility, management experience, and user satisfaction. Optimize Software Stack​ Leverage the opportunity to audit and rationalize existing software licensing and support arrangements, identifying candidates for elimination as Windows 11 and Snapdragon-native solutions mature. Adjust Asset Management Strategies​ With the promise of longer device lifecycles, revisit asset depreciation schedules and refresh policies. Consider extending refresh intervals from three to four or even five years for Snapdragon Windows 11 endpoints. Promote Sustainable Lifecycle Management​ Ensure retired devices are captured by certified recycling programs to maximize sustainability benefits and to comply with internal or regulatory environmental standards. Train Your People​ User enablement is critical: new hardware and AI-powered productivity features may require onboarding and proactive support. Incorporate AI-readiness as part of digital upskilling initiatives. Conclusion: Snapdragon + Windows 11—A Strategic Alliance for the Modern Enterprise​ The evidence, analyzed critically and measured against independent benchmarks and real-world case studies, makes it clear: the combination of Snapdragon processors and Windows 11 can deliver meaningful reductions in IT costs and significantly extend the productive lifespan of enterprise devices. These benefits, however, accrue most fully to organizations that approach refresh and deployment strategically, with a clear eye to compatibility, user enablement, and ongoing technology adoption. For those decision-makers ready to future-proof their fleets—balancing security, sustainability, user experience, and operational efficiency—Snapdragon-powered Windows 11 devices represent an investment not simply in hardware, but in organizational capacity, agility, and resilience for years to come. content: Crypto market analyst CasiTrades has published a detailed technical analysis concerning XRP’s current price structure. She warned of a potential volatility driven by rising funding rates without a significant price rally. The analysis, shared on June 11, highlights the growing risk conditions emerging within XRP’s ongoing consolidation phase. According to the post, XRP is nearing the apex of its macro consolidation zone, with price trading just above key support levels. Despite this support holding for now, funding rates are gradually rising without confirmation of any meaningful breakout. At the time of the analysis, the XRP perpetual futures funding rate had reached 0.01% per eight hours, a subtle but important metric suggesting increasing leverage on the long side. CasiTrades cautions that if funding continues to rise toward 0.02% or higher while price remains stagnant, a downside liquidity event becomes increasingly likely. XRP Funding Rising, While Prices Stall We’re just days away from the apex of #XRP ’s macro consolidation and price is hovering above support, while funding quietly climbs. That’s a dangerous combo. As of this morning, funding rates are ticking up to 0.01%/8h without any… pic.twitter.com/bjKCYk3PiZ — CasiTrades (@CasiTrades) June 11, 2025 Support Levels at Risk as Liquidity Threatens Longs The core of the concern lies in the disparity between increasing open interest and flat price action. Algorithms and market makers closely monitor these conditions, and when long positions become overcrowded and under-protected, it often leads to a rapid downside move designed to flush leveraged positions. In such a scenario, XRP could test lower support levels. The chart attached by the analyst outlines $2.25 as a critical support zone. A failure to maintain that level would expose XRP to deeper pullbacks, with targets at $2.01, $1.90, and potentially $1.55. These levels align with key Fibonacci retracement zones and past liquidity pools, as shown on the 4-hour chart. We are on twitter, follow us to connect with us :- @TimesTabloid1 — TimesTabloid (@TimesTabloid1) July 15, 2023 Wave 3 Outlook Remains Intact Despite Short-Term Threats CasiTrades does not present this potential drop as bearish in the broader context. Instead, the analysis suggests that such a liquidity sweep could generate the necessary momentum for a significant breakout in what appears to be an emerging Wave 3 of a larger Elliott Wave structure. The chart illustrates a projected wave path extending from current consolidation toward higher Fibonacci extensions, notably the 1.618 level at approximately $3.77, and ultimately targeting a wave (4) peak above $4.00. Technical Indicators Signal Caution Ahead While the market remains in a holding pattern, the analyst emphasizes that volatility is “nearly inevitable.” Whether this comes in the form of a final downward flush or a direct breakout from current levels, the implication is that XRP’s next major move could define the trajectory for the remainder of the summer. A potential bearish divergence was also noted in the RSI indicator on the lower panel of the chart, further supporting the case for caution in the near term. This divergence, coupled with rising funding and stagnant price movement, forms the technical basis for the warning issued. CasiTrades’ analysis reinforces the importance of closely monitoring funding rates, support levels, and market positioning in the days ahead. Traders are advised to remain cautious as XRP approaches the climax of its consolidation, where the outcome could dictate both near-term corrections and the start of a new impulsive phase.
